content:
marco: Heads-up: QuarryCorp onboarding; electron desktop client + background telemetry worker are triggering a preflight/handshake surge during app resume. They're hitting sustained 429s right after the app wakes. Logs attached.

marco: ```
[2026-03-30T09:02:11Z] main-process init /v1/preflight 200
[2026-03-30T09:02:12Z] bg-worker-1 init /v1/preflight 429 x 13
[2026-03-30T09:02:12Z] bg-worker-2 auth_refresh /v1/token 429 x 7
[2026-03-30T09:02:13Z] renderer init /v1/preflight 429 x 9
[2026-03-30T09:02:14Z] main-process heartbeat /v1/heartbeat 200
```

tess: They mentioned using server-issued long-lived JWTs that the client refreshes on resume. Several processes race to refresh at the same time. Also their backend mints tokens synchronously and isn't splaying requests.

noah: That pattern creates two hotspots: preflight route (many inits) and auth mint endpoint (concurrent token creation). We should recommend client+server mitigations and offer a fast ops tweak.

marco: Suggested customer-side fixes I'm drafting: 1) switch to short-lived session tokens (60s) minted from backend, 2) on resume, do a single token refresh per renderer/process using a shared in-memory lease (e.g., file lock / cross-process guard), 3) implement exponential backoff with jitter for init and token refresh. Example snippet for exponential backoff + jitter: ```js
async function initWithBackoff(attempt=0){ const max=5; const base=200; const jitter=() => Math.floor(Math.random()*(base*Math.pow(2,attempt))); try { await sdk.init(); } catch(e){ if (attempt>=max) throw e; const wait = base*Math.pow(2,attempt) + jitter(); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, wait)); return initWithBackoff(attempt+1); } }
```

noah: Also advise a single cross-process guard for token minting in Electron: use an OS-level lock or atomic file write that other processes check before minting. Pseudo: ```js
if (fs.existsSync('/tmp/quarry_token_lease')) { await waitForLeaseRelease(); } else { fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/quarry_token_lease', process.pid); try { const t = await mintToken(); } finally { fs.unlinkSync('/tmp/quarry_token_lease'); } }
```

marco: For immediate relief we can apply server-side changes: 1) enable tenant token_mint_coalesce for "quarrycorp" so multiple concurrent mint attempts are collapsed into one backend mint, 2) add a 3s smoothing window (leaky-bucket) on /v1/token for their tenant, 3) temporarily bump preflight burst allowance by +150 tokens for 45m.

rl-bot: RateLimitMonitor: tenant="quarrycorp" spike detected 2026-03-30T09:02:10Z..2026-03-30T09:10:00Z peak_preflight=132 req/min, peak_token_mint=86 req/min. Recommended: token_mint_coalesce=true, preflight_burst=+150, token_leaky_window=3000ms.

tess: QuarryCorp is OK to get temporary server changes while they land the client guard. They want a short maintenance window and step-by-step for the cross-process guard example.

noah: I'll file the infra change for coalesce + burst bump with TTL=45m and ping infra-oncall. Also will watch 429s and token_mint latencies. If 429s persist after client changes, escalate to runtime team for KV-cache and batching analysis.

marco: Post-rollout checklist for CS: 1) monitor tenant 429s for 2 hours, 2) verify token header varies per process (short-lived), 3) collect 8 init traces and 5 mint traces, 4) confirm cross-process lease prevents concurrent mints. If mint route still shows spikes, we'll provide a tiny mint proxy example to coalesce at the customer side.

marco: Sending guidance and snippets to the customer now. Will update the onboarding ticket and loop SE for the maintenance window. Thanks all.
